title: Step 1
criteria:
## Required Features

- A single downward-pointing triangle.
- A long horizontal top edge and two diagonal edges that meet at the bottom point.

## Reject If

- A square or diamond.
- An upward-pointing triangle.
- Extra visible flaps that break the simple triangular silhouette.

title: Step 2
criteria:
## Required Features

- An upright kite or diamond with top, bottom, left, and right points.
- Both narrow front flaps are clearly visible and folded inward to meet along the vertical center near the bottom.

## Reject If

- Either front flap remains open to the side instead of being folded inward to the center.
- A plain kite or diamond without the two narrow center flaps.

title: Step 3
criteria:
## Required Features

- A diamond with a clear horizontal crease across the middle and its bottom point visible inside the camera frame.
- Two narrow upright flaps that are fully visible and rise from the middle crease to the top center.

## Reject If

- A closed kite or diamond without the horizontal middle crease.
- A model without both narrow top-center flaps.

title: Step 4
criteria:
## Required Features

- A large lower diamond with a horizontal crease across the middle.
- Two distinct, broad triangular side flaps opened outward and upward: one to the left and one to the right.
- A narrow upright flap separated at the top center.
- A wide, roughly symmetric crown formed by the three flaps.

## Reject If

- A plain diamond.
- A narrow or asymmetric cluster of mostly upright top flaps.
- Overlapping top flaps.
- Either side flap still folded toward the center or not clearly projecting outward.

title: Step 5
criteria:
## Candidate Paper

- The candidate is folded from paper whose two faces have visibly different colors.

## Required Visual Evidence

- The candidate must show one large central diamond in an opposite-face color that is clearly different from the background crown. If this contrasting central diamond is absent, return false.
- The central diamond consists of one broad upward-pointing triangle and one broad downward-pointing triangle that share the same straight, crosswise crease.
- The upper triangle's sharp apex reaches the lowest point of the crown's central split. The multi-pointed crown remains visible behind it.
- The entire central diamond, including its apex, outer edges, shared crease, and bottom tip, is clearly visible.

## Allowed Variations

- Exact colors are irrelevant. Any two clearly different paper-face colors are valid.
- Minor asymmetry, modest rotation, or perspective tilt. Interpret directions relative to the model.

## Return False If

- The crown and lower center show only the same paper-face color. Shadows or lighter and darker shades of one color do not count as the opposite face.
- There is only a broad downward-pointing face beneath the crown; a narrow upright center flap does not complete the broad central diamond.
- A hand or another object overlaps the central diamond, its apex or shared crease, or the crown's central split, or substantially covers the crown.
- An additional horizontal band truncates the upper half of the diamond, or its sharp upper apex is folded down.

title: Step 6
criteria:
## Candidate Paper

- The candidate is folded from paper whose two faces have visibly different colors.

## Required Visual Evidence

- The candidate must show an opposite-face crown with a tall center point and separate left and right side points above a broad body of the other paper face.
- A shallow folded strip of the body face spans the upper body. Its visible surface forms a band between the crown and a straight crosswise lower crease. A crease line by itself does not count as a band.
- A short body-face triangle rises from the band's upper edge at the center, in front of the crown.
- Below the band, the broad body ends in a long downward point.

## Allowed Variations

- Minor asymmetry, modest rotation or perspective, and variations in the band's thickness or alignment. Exact colors are irrelevant.

## Return False If

- A broad or tall body-face upward triangle fills the center from one crosswise crease toward the crown's central split. Together with the downward body it forms a central diamond; it is not a band even if the crease resembles one.
- A hand or finger is actively folding or pressing the paper, or overlaps the middle band or its boundaries. A nearby hand that does not overlap the paper remains acceptable.
- The folded band, its short center triangle, or the long downward-pointing body is absent or not clearly visible.
- The long downward body is folded upward or tucked away.

title: Step 7
criteria:
## Required Features

- A completed multi-pointed crown with a tall center point and separate left and right points rises above a short, wide folded base.
- No long body, large diamond, or downward-pointing flap extends below the base.

## Acceptable Views

- Front, tilted, or nearly edge-on. Crown layers may overlap, and the base may look like a shallow trapezoid, a broad shallow triangle, a thin wedge, or an open triangular gap.
- The base may bow open; it does not need to be pressed flat or closed.
- The crown and the broad, shallow central part of the base provide the step-specific visual evidence; outer-end details do not distinguish this completed fold.

## Reject If

- A large downward-pointing body remains below the crown instead of the required short, wide base.
